indexing.note: fixed by statute (30 Del. C. 1102(a)(14) bands, same since 2000)
fixed by statute: 3,250 / 6,500 and the 2,500 age-65 addition (30 Del. C. 1108(a)(3), (b))
scheduled: military pension cap 12,500 through 2026, 15,000 for 2027, 20,000 for 2028, 25,000 from 2029 (30 Del. C. 1106(b)(3)b.-e.)
fixed by statute: 12,500 (30 Del. C. 1106(b)(3)b.2); from 2027 a military pension gets the greater of 12,500 and the military schedule, which is not grown here
fixed by statute: 110 per exemption and 110 at age 60 (30 Del. C. 1110(b))

not_modelled.what: Line 11 exclusion for persons 60 or over or disabled (2,000 single or separate, Line 10 of 10,000 or less, earned income under 2,500; 4,000 joint, both spouses 60 or disabled, Line 10 of 20,000 or less, combined earned income under 5,000). Left out because it does not change the tax of an age-qualified filer: at Line 10 of 10,000 a single filer aged 60 owes 134.25 on 6,750 after the standard deduction, less than the 220 of personal credits (110 + 110 at 60 or over); a joint couple both 60 at Line 10 of 20,000 owes 429 on 13,500, less than their 440 of credits. It matters only for a disabled filer under 60, which a projection does not know.

Higher-education exclusion (Line 8a): IRA, 401(k) and 457 distributions used the same year for books, tuition or fees of the taxpayer or dependents under 26. A projection does not know what a withdrawal pays for.
Interest on U.S. obligations (Treasury bills, notes, bonds, savings bonds) is exempt (Line 5). A projection cannot tell Treasury interest from other interest.
Additional standard deduction of 2,500 for a blind person (Line 21). A projection does not know blindness.
The 110 personal credit for each dependent listed on the federal return (Line 27a); the filer's and spouse's credits are modelled.

approximations.what: The Delaware standard deduction (and the age-65 additional amount, which needs it) is always taken; Delaware itemized deductions (Form PIT-RSA) are not modelled.
approximations.size: Up to 6.6% of the amount by which itemized deductions exceed the standard and additional amounts, for an itemizer.

approximations.what: Roth conversions are left out of the 60-plus pension exclusion (the booklet does not say whether they count as eligible retirement income).
approximations.size: Only when the person's pension and other eligible income leave room under 12,500: up to 6.6% x 12,500 = 825 a year per person.

approximations.what: For a person under 60, IRA and 401(k) distributions, annuities and Roth conversions are left out of the 2,000 non-military pension exclusion (the booklet speaks only of a pension).
approximations.size: Up to 6.6% x 2,000 = 132 a year per person, for someone under 60 with such income and no pension.

approximations.what: Annuities (outside a qualified plan) are left out of the 60-plus pension exclusion (not named in the booklet).
approximations.size: Only when room remains under 12,500: up to 825 a year per person.

approximations.what: The rule that an early distribution (1099-R Box 7 code 1, or one with a federal early-withdrawal penalty) does not qualify is not applied; every covered pension of a person under 60 gets the exclusion.
approximations.size: Up to 6.6% x 2,000 = 132 a year (non-military) or 6.6% x 12,500 = 825 (military), for an under-60 pension paid as an early distribution.

approximations.what: A projection that cannot tell Delaware bonds from other states' bonds treats all tax-exempt interest as other-state and adds it back (Line 2).
approximations.size: Up to 6.6% of the interest from Delaware obligations.

approximations.what: Treasury interest is taxed (the Line 5 subtraction is not modelled).
approximations.size: Up to 6.6% of the Treasury interest.

approximations.what: The credit for income tax paid to another state (Line 28) is not modelled.
approximations.size: Up to the other state's tax on income it taxes, for a household with income taxed elsewhere.

approximations.what: The separate tax on a qualified lump-sum distribution (Form PIT-STC, 30 Del. C. §1102(b)) is not used; any lump sum runs through the schedule.
approximations.size: Only in a year with a qualified lump-sum distribution.

approximations.what: Tax is computed from the statute's rate schedule; returns with Line 23 under 60,000 use the Division's tax table, which is built on the same rates but in income rows.
approximations.size: A few dollars at most (rounding within a table row).

approximations.what: Later years: the United States military pension exclusion rises to 15,000 (2027), 20,000 (2028) and 25,000 (2029 on), for those under 60 and, as the greater of it and the 12,500 exclusion, for those 60 and older (30 Del. C. 1106(b)(3)c.-e., SB 219). The projection keeps 12,500.
approximations.size: From 2029, up to 12,500 x 6.6% = 825 a year per military retiree.
